observation.visible_scene: A night-time outdoor shot of two date-palm trees, each completely wrapped in strings of small addressable LED lights, set against a black sky with dim shrubbery along the bottom and a small leafy plant at the right edge; a 'twinkly PRO' watermark sits in the lower-right corner. The trees themselves do not move; the only visible activity is the dynamic recoloring of the lights in chase/wipe patterns.
visible_changes: At t=0 the left tree glows mostly red (trunk and fronds) while the right tree has a white trunk with blue-and-white fronds.
From t≈0.08 to t≈0.5 a bright white segment climbs the left trunk from bottom to top, and the left fronds change from all-red to white-centre fronds with red outer edges.
Over the same early interval the right tree's trunk and fronds settle into a solid blue.
From t≈0.5 to t≈1.5 the left tree holds white fronds with red edges plus a thin red streak running down one side of an otherwise white trunk, while the right tree stays blue.
Beginning around t≈1.25, red/pink pixels appear on the right tree's left fronds and spread across its fronds and trunk, converting the right tree from blue to red by t≈1.8–2.0.
Concurrently (t≈1.8–2.3) a blue streak climbs the left trunk and then spreads into the left fronds, turning the left tree blue by t≈2.3–3.0.
From t≈2.3 to t≈3.1 the left tree is blue (with some white on its right fronds) and the right tree is red.
Near the end (t≈3.1–3.33) a white streak climbs the right tree's trunk and right fronds, a chase pattern still in progress at the last frame.
The two trunks keep the same relative left/right positions throughout; no physical swaying or object motion is evident, only light-pattern changes.
outside_clip_unknowns: The light state before t=0 and after t=3.33 (the segment ends mid-chase on the right tree).
Whether the colour program loops or continues into other patterns.
What controller or trigger drives the colour changes.
uncertain_details: A slight upward/leftward shift of the trees in the frame may indicate minor handheld camera drift, but the dark background gives too little reference to confirm it.
The exact hue of the 'blue' channel (blue vs violet) and whether some streaks are travelling up or down is partly ambiguous due to motion blur and low light.
The thin red line on the left trunk between t≈0.5–1.5 appears largely static rather than moving, which is not fully certain.
